title: prefill-decode-chunked-speculative-stage-overlap-kernel-scheduler-kv-cache-optimizations
author: Rohit Patel
description: Context: Prefill vs decode pipeline had growing tail latency and suboptimal GPU utilization for mixed short/long sequences. This PR introduces an end-to-end set of runtime optimizations: chunked prefill with speculative execution, stage-overlap prefill/decode scheduling, an improved kernel selection heuristic in the kernel scheduler, and tighter KV cache management to reduce memory churn. Motivation: reduce median and tail latency for customer workloads while improving throughput and keeping per-token cost stable. Design: 1) Chunked prefill breaks long prefill sequences into configurable chunks to enable early decode overlap and reduce peak GPU memory usage. 2) Speculative prefill runs an optimistic partial prefill+decode for likely next-token prefixes and rolls back cheaply on mismatch to reduce decode stalls. 3) Stage overlap scheduler allows prefill and decode stages to execute concurrently on disjoint resources where possible; scheduler now tracks per-request resource footprints and prioritizes overlap-safe tasks. 4) Kernel scheduler heuristic updated to prefer fused attention kernels for medium sequence lengths and to pre-select quantized kernels when cache hit rate indicates stability. 5) KV cache manager avoids aggressive eviction during chunked prefill by applying a short-lived pin for recently used prefixes and tracks cache-locality per-batch to improve reuse. Testing: microbenchmarks, large-scale perf canary runs, unit/integration tests added for chunking, speculative rollback, and cache pin semantics. Results: end-to-end synthetic perf shows 18-26% improvement in median latency and 22-33% reduction in 95th/99th tail latency for mixed workloads; throughput improvement of 10-15% under high concurrency. Backwards compatibility: feature gated behind runtime flag and rollout config; default disabled for customers on older Dedicated hardware until validated. Migrations: no API changes to external API, internal config toggles documented.

add speculative prefill executor and rollback path

review_comments: Maya Thompson: Can you quantify memory overhead introduced by speculative prefill under peak load? Suggest adding a soft cap and metrics.
Rohit Patel (author): Added a short-lived pin and a soft global speculative budget metric; updated cache_manager to emit speculative_memory_bytes and the perf canary includes the budget test.
Carlos Rivera: Kernel heuristic looks promising but add unit tests to ensure fallback to baseline kernels on numeric regressions.
Rohit Patel (author): Added unit tests and extended the kernel selection simulation to run against fp16/quantized kernels and compare outputs within tolerance.
Elena Ivanova: Please ensure rollout is gated and document how to disable on Dedicated clusters; add an integration test for rollback correctness.
Rohit Patel (author): Added runtime flag runtime.features.prefill_speculative and documented console toggle; added integration rollback test to CI.
release_notes: Runtime: Add chunked and speculative prefill with stage-overlap scheduler and KV-cache pinning. Improves latency and throughput for mixed-length workloads. Feature behind runtime flag and rolled out gradually.
merge_summary: Merged to main after perf canary and two approvals. Rollout gated via runtime flag; disabled by default for older Dedicated hardware. Monitored metrics include median/tail latency, speculative_memory_bytes, and kv_cache_hit_rate.
